entries.new: A relative window such as 近三年 means the 36 months up to the latest data point; state its start and end dates on the page.

entries.old: Use chart_type='choropleth' to show one value per country on a map (for example a World Bank indicator across countries or territories). It requires category_field, value_field, and category_names='worldbank' or 'iso3'; category_field joins through the same vendored economy table category_names uses, so every value must be an exact World Bank name or ISO3 code, never a paraphrase. It supports at most 60 rows (filter upstream in SQL), rejects regional/income-group aggregates (for example Sub-Saharan Africa or World) and any economy the basemap has no feature for, and rejects duplicate economies. It draws its own locator inset and does not support reference_line or range_bracket annotations. Set inset={iso3:[...]} to zoom a manual list of small economies into their own panel, or inset={auto:true} to let the renderer pick which ones are too small to label on the main map.

entries.old: Never translate a place name yourself. If a chart's category_field, facet_field, or series_field holds World Bank English country/region names or ISO3 codes and the chart's language is 'zh', set category_names='worldbank' or 'iso3' so the renderer shows the vendored, provenance-recorded localized name instead; lint blocks any value that table cannot resolve.
entries.new: Never translate a place name yourself. If a chart's category_field, facet_field, or series_field holds World Bank English country/region names or ISO3 codes and the chart's language is 'zh', set category_names='worldbank' or 'iso3' so the renderer shows the vendored, provenance-recorded localized name instead; lint blocks any value that table cannot resolve. On zh pages a country name field is the ISO3 code column with category_names='iso3' (ISO2 codes: 'iso2') and a currency name field is the ISO 4217 code column with category_names='iso4217'; drop aggregate rows (OWID_*, regions, income groups) in SQL, and never type a translated name.

Use chart_type='strip_plot' for the spread and extremes of many units inside groups: category_field is the group (one chart row each, at most 40), value_field is the unit's value with one SQL row per unit (at most 600), and label_field names the units so label_extremes can label the highest and lowest across the chart.

Use chart_type='stacked_bar_100' for the shares of a whole across many entities with one highlighted segment: it requires unit='%', category_field (the entity, at most 25), series_field (the segments, at most 5) and value_field, every entity's shares summing to 100 (+/- 1); set highlight_segment, and sort='desc' to order the bars by it.

Use chart_type='mirrored_bar' for a two-sided distribution such as a male/female age pyramid: category_field is the band (at most 25), series_field has exactly 2 values (the two sides), value_field is at least 0, and an optional period_field with at most 2 values adds a comparison period; sort and annotations are not supported.

entries.old: Optional per-field measure declarations (field, unit, measure_kind). A count or calendar-year value_field is spelled as a plain integer.
entries.new: Per-field measure declarations. A count or calendar-year value_field is spelled as a plain integer.

args.description: strip_plot: units named chart-wide, half highest and half lowest (default 4; needs label_field)
stacked_bar_100: series_field values left to right
stacked_bar_100: segment whose value orders the bars (direction from sort)
stacked_bar_100: segment drawn in the accent colour, the rest grey
mirrored_bar: series_field value on the left (default: first in row order)
mirrored_bar: optional field holding at most 2 periods to compare

slope only: set when start_field and end_field hold ranks (1 = best, positive integers; an empty end means outside the ranking). Draws a bump chart with rank 1 on top, one row per rank up to N, and anyone outside the top N on an N+1 row with their true rank.

small_multiples line only: set when value_field is an index rebased to this value (for example 100): one x value (the base period) must equal it in every panel, so rebase in SQL. Draws a base line labelled with that period, y tick labels and an end value in each panel.

entries.new: The first content module after the title and dek is a hero_stat bound with value_from when the story has one prominent verified number; otherwise it is the lead visual. Never open with a text module or a pull quote.
A hero_stat label names the subject, the measure and the period, for example 「2024年阿根廷年通胀率」, not 「通胀率」.

entries.old: Create an observable editorial visualization plan. A system-verified claim_id produces a publishable plan; omitting claim_id produces an explicitly non-publishable draft. The model cannot select verification status. Supports statistical charts plus flows, networks, hierarchies, temporal structures, spatial flows and explanatory process graphics.
